baselineRegression.method: Identical final component tests against isolated turn-start LegalHub. Nine parameterized failures are not nine separate defects.

diffCheck: passed with repository CRLF whitespace settings
changes: Organization create/update/delete/material writes now use one scope-owned serial queue and server-confirmed case snapshot. Pending field edits merge into the current UI state, and failed patches are discarded after the queue drains.
Older list reads are aborted by writes. Refresh waits for the queued writes before reading; queued operations check their original owner signal before sending.

Create/delete no longer rebuild the organization list from a captured render snapshot. Personal create/delete read the latest local store. Organization material records use the server result instead of synthetic frontend IDs and optimistic append/rollback.
Empty successful mutation responses are rejected. Material persistence is reflected in the list only after confirmation.

Removed duplicate workflow-order declaration/sorting and separate readiness done flags. Readiness text is assembled once instead of up to eleven repeated assemblies. Existing labels, predicates, statuses, navigation order and actions remain equivalent.
Updated old mocked mutation responses to match real route return shapes, and removed one source-string DELETE assertion now covered by actual component request-order and deletion assertions.
preserved: Original organization HTTP routes, request authorization and ACL, case IDs, local persistence schema and tool behavior.
Immediate field typing feedback; accepted patches retain typed whitespace until refresh.
Unrelated reminder/plan requests remain outside the case-write queue.
All earlier uncommitted changes and real user data.
limitations: Queue is scoped to one mounted LegalHub. This is not a cross-client lock, database transaction or rollback of server writes. A failed/aborted response can occur after a server write.
Keystroke writes are ordered but not debounced or coalesced; this batch does not claim reduced API volume or lower model latency.

Component HTTP is mocked; backend permission/database regressions use isolated data. No real model invocation, native-client UI acceptance or full-suite rerun. Frontend-only edits did not require another backend build.
Material callback consumers that ignore persistence results, legacy personal data account isolation, multi-entry model endpoint persistence and remaining program zones are still open.
No commit, push or client restart.
